newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia C.bank holds 400 T gold, state stocks empty.
newsitem.headline: Russia C.bank holds 400 T gold, state stocks empty.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank's gold reserves are about 400 tonnes, and state strategic reserves, known as GosFond or GosKhran, are nearly depleted, central bank deputy press service director Natalya Khomenko said on Friday.

"Yes, our reserves are about 400 tonnes," she said. Asked about the state's strategic reserves, which are separate from the bank's reserves, she said, "To all appearances there is little there, but this can be explained by a change in the way gold reserves are formed."

She said the near-depletion of strategic stockpile reserves did not mean that Russia as a whole had no gold."Gold is not leaving the country," she said. She added later, "We (the central bank) bought those reserves that were in Goskhran (GosFond)."
Khomenko could not say how much the bank had bought. She said Central Bank reserves were used to defend the rouble and GosFond (GosKhran) reserves had a "stockpile" function.
A source in the Audit Chamber told Reuters earlier on Friday that to a chamber report completed in September 1996 showed that Russia's state stocks of gold were practically empty.
Asked about the report, Khomenko said that it was correct, reiterating that reserves from GosFond (GosKhran) were exhausted because the bank had bought them.
